correctness.rationale: In any connected proper-interval ordering v_1,…,v_n with umbrella property, closed neighborhoods are contiguous integer intervals [ℓ_i,r_i] and both endpoint sequences are nondecreasing. Starting at extreme v1, distance layers L_k are contiguous cliques indexed by successive b_{k+1}=r_{b_k}; stability of rooted 1-WL separates each distance layer. For each nonroot vertex in layer k, predecessor-layer neighbor count is b_{k−1}−ℓ_i+1, successor count is r_i−b_k (final layer has r_i=n), uniquely determining its full closed neighborhood. Thus equal colors iff true twins except the distinguished root, and refinement needs at most D+1 rounds. True-twin clique cells have uniform full/empty bipartite interactions, so C²-equivalent arbitrary rooted graphs must realize exactly the same cell sizes and quotients; hence rooted identification. Root-fixing automorphisms are independent permutations on nonroot twin cells. Any doubly stochastic root-fixing matrix commuting with adjacency preserves 1-WL cells (strict convexity level-set argument), hence decomposes into those Birkhoff blocks; conversely every such block commutes. Independently enumerated all 6,918 connected proper-interval right-endpoint encodings at n≤10, checked actual individualization refinement versus nonroot true-twin equality and stabilization bound, and the three-path center root counterexample. Finite checks corroborate all-size layer proof.
